notes.observation: The first extraction unit begins by repeating the chapter title '"சிவாய நம! ஓம் நமசிவாய"'.
notes.translation_action: Represent the title in chapter metadata and do not duplicate the extraction heading as body prose.

notes.observation: The first extraction unit ends with 'நாலு பெரிய மனிதர்கள் இருக்குமிடத்தில்' and the next begins 'சட்டை போட்டுக்கொண்டு போகமுடியாது.' The sentence is continuous across the source-unit boundary.
notes.translation_action: Translate continuously; do not treat the JSON boundary as authorial paragraphing.

notes.observation: A later unit ends with 'அத்தகைய உணர்விலே மதிமயங்கித்' and the following unit continues 'திருக்குவளை செல்லும் வழியிலே போய்க் கொண்டிருக்கிறேன்.'
notes.translation_action: Reconstruct the continuous sentence/movement before translating.

notes.observation: The travel-memory section contains several further extraction-boundary continuations, including 'அப்படிப்' + 'போகும்போது' and 'அடியெடுத்து வைத்ததே' + 'கிடையாதே!'.
notes.translation_action: Treat these as page/extraction joins, not deliberate authorial breaks; preserve traceability in alignment.

notes.observation: A long first-person journey through Thirukkuvalai is presented through extended quoted/oral recollection spanning multiple extraction units, with repeated direct demonstratives such as 'இதோ' and 'அதோ'. Source-unit boundaries and quotation marks do not define reliable literary paragraphs.
notes.translation_action: Reconstruct English paragraphs around the spoken journey's rhetorical units while preserving the repeated 'Here/There' quality and oral flow.

notes.observation: The source reads 'நாள் கூட அப்போதெல்லாம் நம்பித்தான் நடுங்கிக் கொண்டிருந்தேன்' immediately after Kalaignar explains that many still reject the natural explanation for the mysterious lights. Context strongly requires the first-person sense 'நான்கூட' ('I too') rather than literal 'நாள் கூட'.
notes.translation_action: Render the clear contextual first-person sense ('I too, in those days...') and keep this source form disclosed. Do not alter the read-only source.

notes.observation: The form 'வேணடுமென்ற' occurs in the Angalamman temple passage and is evidently a transposed/defective extraction of the ordinary contextual form 'வேண்டுமென்ற'.
notes.translation_action: Translate the contextual sense and retain this note rather than silently treating the extraction as clean.

notes.observation: The remembered school expression 'அரிநமோத்து சிந்தம்' is independently attested in Tamil descriptions of older education-initiation practice. A separate memoir places the same formula at the ceremonial beginning of learning immediately before the first letter is written in sand; the Tamil Digital Library text 'தமிழலங்காரம்' also preserves the traditional formula/near-variant in an old invocation context.
notes.translation_action: Retain Kalaignar's Tamilised form as 'Arinamothu Sindham' and identify it minimally as an old initiation formula. Do not silently Sanskritise it or impose a speculative word-for-word doctrinal translation.

notes.observation: Postmaster Iyer calls across the pond: 'தபால் வந்திருக்கு நோக்கு!'. In this speaker context, 'நோக்கு' is the dated Brahmin-Tamil pronominal form of 'உனக்கு' ('for/to you'), not the ordinary verb 'look'. Tamil Lexicon records this dialectal pronoun use.
notes.translation_action: Correct T1's 'The mail's come, look!' to 'Mail has come for you!' Preserve the social/dialect function without inventing an English regional accent.

notes.observation: In 'பாழடைந்து, நிறமிழந்து, பெரிய உருவமொன்று மூளியாக உட்கார்ந்திருக்கிறதே', Tamil Lexicon senses of 'மூளி' include deformed/defective or a thing with a part missing or broken.
notes.translation_action: Use a source-near damaged/mutilated description rather than T1's added image 'like a broken hulk'.

notes.observation: Tamil Lexicon records 'கதுப்பு' both as cheek and as the fleshy part of a fruit beside the seed. This supports Kalaignar's concrete comparison 'மாம்பழக் கதுப்புப் போன்ற கன்னம்'.
notes.translation_action: Render the comparison as cheeks like the fleshy sides of a mango rather than abstracting it to generic plumpness.

notes.observation: The chapter contains ritual and social vocabulary including வைதிக, வித்யாரம்பம், காணிக்கை, mantra belief, caste-coded clothing practices, அக்கிரகாரம், village deities and local ritual customs.
notes.translation_action: Translate or lightly gloss according to context without turning the prose into ethnographic explanation. Preserve Kalaignar's own later critical/rationalist stance rather than adding the translator's judgement.

notes.observation: The social-criticism passage contrasts upper-caste reform ideas with 'புனுகு' applied to an unhealed wound and revolutionary voices with surgery that can heal it; it also uses the kicked-ball image for oppressed people rising with greater force.
notes.translation_action: Preserve the concrete wound/punugu, surgery and kicked-ball images rather than replacing them with abstract political summary.

notes.observation: The homecoming passage says relatives 'உச்சிமோந்து' him. Tamil Lexicon defines 'உச்சிமோத்தல்' as smelling the crown of a child's head out of affection.
notes.translation_action: Retain the specific affectionate gesture in English rather than silently replacing it with a generic kiss.

notes.observation: The chapter moves rapidly among ritual childhood, comic theft, caste humiliation, social revolt, childhood theatre, nostalgia, superstition, later rationalist explanation, village humour, grief for the dead and affection for home.
notes.translation_action: Preserve these changes of register. Do not regularise the chapter into a single solemn rationalist or nostalgic voice.

notes.observation: Several jokes depend on timing: the thief who steals the carefully preserved pot of hair thinking it is a money-box, the father's chicken appetite producing an Angalamman puja, and soil thrown to curse another family sometimes blowing back into the devotees' own eyes.
notes.translation_action: Preserve punchline timing and do not explain the jokes after translating them.

notes.observation: No Wikisource maintenance/editorial unit comparable to the two exclusions in v1-ch02 is present in the inspected v1-ch03 source body.
notes.translation_action: No non-authorial body exclusion is required for this chapter.
